verdicts.reason: A puts the can at the top and sinks the quote to the bottom, where its right half sits on the faint circle. This reverses the original's quote-then-product order and leaves a dead gap mid-canvas. B keeps the quote-then-can order and a cleaner top block. Both shrink the quote so it barely outweighs the caps attribution, B's can only grazes the circle instead of sitting in it, and B leaves a lot of empty space below.

A has the same inverted order as pair 1 A: logo, then can, then the quote marooned at the bottom over the circle. Its narrower wrap also leaves an awkward 'a little / bitter' break. B (identical to pair 1 B) reads quote-then-product as the original does, but the headline is undersized against the attribution and the bottom third is mostly empty circle.

A (same layout as the B candidates above) is coherent but has a weak quote hierarchy and a lot of empty space at the bottom. B crams the small quote against the top edge, leaves a big gap between the can and the circle, and drops the logo onto the circle's edge so it straddles two backgrounds. That is an unintended collision, and the logo looks like an afterthought.
